Simulations, Models, Twins
Upper Manhattan / NYC

Street tree
stormwater
interception
simulation

An attempt to visualize how street trees act as a network to mitigate stormwater runoff. This uses a simplified version of NYC Parks’ methodology, which uses the USDA Forest Service’s i-Tree software.

The record / 2015

Street trees and planting sites from the 2015 census, situated within 2010 census blocks. The clock applies growth, mortality and planting assumptions to this record.

The rule / annual interception

canopy × rainfall × 0.0254
× interception × 264.17
= US gallons per year

Canopy is a circle: π × (crown diameter / 2)². Crown is in meters; rainfall is in inches. Conversion factors are specified in the project prompt.

Limitations & assumptions

This estimates rainfall intercepted by trees, rather than runoff avoided at a drain. It uses a uniform interception fraction and does not account for drainage, topography, canopy overlap, seasonal foliage, rainfall intensity, or networks of policy and care.

Deaths and planting sites are selected with repeatable random draws. Only the original dead trees and stumps are available for planting; a planted site stays occupied even if its tree dies. Each planting is a honeylocust with a 3-inch DBH, as specified in the prompt.

Species without an equation use an agreed same-genus proxy, then honeylocust. Age estimates cap their DBH input at the supplied x_max; this does not cap the measured DBH used for crowns or future growth. Growth is the difference between the DBH predictions at estimated age + 1 and estimated age. These empirical equations may behave poorly beyond their observed sizes.

All 12,715 records are retained. The 267 points outside the supplied census blocks appear in the tree view but are excluded from block sums. One living tree has an invalid diameter: its crown, age, growth and interception remain unknown, and it is excluded from mortality simulation. Four additional living trees have nonphysical negative crown predictions in 2015. Negative or undefined crown predictions remain unknown in every year; undefined growth leaves the previous DBH intact. Trees with unknown interception appear as white outlined points. Blocks with no modeled interception are outlined without a fill.

Data & citations
  1. NYC Parks, TreesCount! 2015 — supplied Upper Manhattan subset: 12,094 living trees, 388 dead trees and 233 stumps.
  2. NYC Department of City Planning, 2010 Census Blocks — supplied subset of 580 polygons. The exact download and clipping history were not recorded.
  3. USDA Forest Service, Urban Tree Database — supplied Queens equations for 21 species, attributed to Table S6, Northeast (2005). Equation forms follow Table S4, with January 2020 corrections.
  4. Xiao et al. (2000) — interception measured on two trees in Davis, California; the project uses 15% as a simplified assumption.
  5. NYC Parks, tree benefits — methodological inspiration. The project prompt supplies 41 inches/year, attributed to JFK in 2000; that attribution was not independently verified.
  6. i-Tree Eco Forecast guide — context for mortality and planting. The project's 2.8% and 0.57% mortality assumptions were not verified as i-Tree defaults.
